The other renderers that inherit the permissive default implement both features: DIRECTX9 (SetRenderTargets bounded by D3DCAPS9::NumSimultaneousRTs, D3D9OcclusionQueryRenderer), FNA3D (FNA3D_SetRenderTargets, FNA3D_CreateQuery) and WEBGPU.

issues.title: CNA public headers export Sharp Runtime's unprefixed property macros (YES, NO, nothing, ref1, getter1, CONTAINS, INTERNAL and others)
issues.summary: 99 headers under modules/*/include include SharpRuntime/Prop.hpp or SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp, which define 33 short unprefixed macros, so a game translation unit that includes such a CNA header cannot use those spellings as identifiers.
issues.public_contract: Any CNA public header that includes SharpRuntime/Prop.hpp or SharpRuntime/SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp (for example Viewport.hpp, ContentManager.hpp, SoundEffect.hpp)
issues.expected: Including a framework header should not reserve short, common identifiers in the program's macro namespace; the XNA API a port expects occupies no macro names.
issues.actual: {{src:modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Viewport.hpp|Viewport.hpp}} and {{src:modules/content/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ContentManager.hpp|ContentManager.hpp}} include SharpRuntime/Prop.hpp; {{src:modules/audio/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Audio/SoundEffect.hpp|SoundEffect.hpp}} includes SharpRuntime/SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp; 99 public headers include one of the two. Prop.hpp (sharp-runtime @ 41b918c9, unchanged since 2026-07-25) defines 31 macros, among them YES (1), NO (0), nothing and static0 (empty), ref1 (&), getter1, member0, IF_1 and DEF_PROP; SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp adds CONTAINS(STRING, SUBSTR) and an empty INTERNAL. After such an include, bool NO = false; becomes bool 0 = false; and a variable called nothing disappears.
issues.evidence: Checked by reading at 009d40f5 (a grep of modules/*/include for the two includes) and the two sharp-runtime headers at next @ 41b918c9 in the local checkout (the snapshot pins no revision); not executed. The macros belong to sharp-runtime; the limitation is CNA's because its public headers expose them.

// Illustrative; not compiled.
#include "Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Viewport.hpp"
bool NO = false;        // preprocesses to: bool 0 = false;  -> error
int nothing = 3;        // preprocesses to: int  = 3;        -> error
issues.tests_current: No test includes CNA headers alongside common identifiers or checks the macro namespace.
issues.regression_test: A compile test that includes every public header and then declares the colliding identifiers; the fix is prefixing the macros in sharp-runtime or keeping Prop.hpp out of CNA's public headers.
issues.blast_radius: Game code that uses any of the 33 spellings as an identifier in a translation unit that includes an affected CNA header. Behaviour of CNA itself is unaffected.
issues.workaround: Rename the colliding identifiers, or #undef the macro after the last CNA include.

issues.title: EasyGL GPU timers read 32-bit nanosecond results and cannot detect GL disjoint events
issues.summary: EasyGLGpuTimerRenderer reads GL_TIME_ELAPSED as a 32-bit value because meta-gl offers no 64-bit read or disjoint query, so results saturate near 4.29 s and only an all-ones disjoint result is rejected.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Graphics::GpuTimer and RenderPipeline pass timings (CNAEXT) on the EasyGL GL profiles
issues.expected: GL_EXT_disjoint_timer_query results are read as 64-bit values and believed only after GL_GPU_DISJOINT_EXT reports no disjoint event.
issues.actual: EasyGLGpuTimerRenderer::IsResultAvailable and ElapsedNanoseconds in {{src:modules/renderers/easygl/src/EasyGLRenderer.cpp|EasyGLRenderer.cpp}} read the result with glGetQueryObjectuiv into a 32-bit value and reject only the all-ones saturation value; the in-code comment states that meta-gl offers neither a 64-bit read nor the disjoint query. A reading taken across a disjoint event that is not exactly 0xFFFFFFFF is reported as a duration, and a real pass longer than about 4.29 s saturates.
issues.evidence: Checked by reading at 009d40f5 and meta-gl develop @ 20c8b2dc in the local checkout (no ui64v read and no disjoint token in include/); not executed. The limitation is imposed by the sibling API; the pass durations the engine layer measures are far below the saturation point.
issues.tests_current: {{src:modules/graphics-ext/tests/CNA/Graphics/GpuTimerTests.cpp|GpuTimerTests.cpp}} and PassTimingTests.cpp cover the timer contract; nothing injects a disjoint event.
issues.regression_test: Once meta-gl exposes glGetQueryObjectui64v and GL_GPU_DISJOINT_EXT: a test that a disjoint flag invalidates the sample.
issues.blast_radius: GPU pass timings on the EasyGL family only; the first sample after a context change is the known disjoint case. Rendering is unaffected.
issues.workaround: Treat outlying samples, especially the first after a context change, as invalid.

issues.title: A .cnj Texture2D colorKey applied at load time leaves keyed texels as (key RGB, alpha 0), so SpriteBatch's default AlphaBlend adds the key colour
issues.summary: ContentManager's runtime .cnj route writes Color(keyR, keyG, keyB, 0) into a straight-alpha texture, so under SpriteBatch's premultiplied default blend each keyed texel adds the key colour instead of vanishing.
issues.public_contract: ContentManager::Load<Texture2D>(name) for a .cnj Texture2D document with colorKey; SpriteBatch::Begin() default BlendState::AlphaBlend
issues.expected: XNA's TextureProcessor with ColorKeyEnabled replaces key-coloured texels with transparent black, which is invisible under premultiplied and non-premultiplied blending alike. CNA's own build pipeline reaches the same texel for a .cnj-authored key, because it premultiplies after keying (default premultiplyAlpha true in {{src:modules/content/src/Pipeline/Texture2DContentPipeline.cpp|Texture2DContentPipeline.cpp}}).
issues.actual: The runtime .cnj Texture2D reader in {{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp|ContentManager.cpp}} loads the source image through the loose tier (Texture2D(path, device), straight alpha) and then ApplyColorKey replaces every matching texel with Color(keyR, keyG, keyB, 0). SpriteBatch::Begin() defaults to BlendState::AlphaBlend (One, InverseSourceAlpha), which treats colour as premultiplied: a keyed texel contributes its full key colour and keeps the destination, so a magenta key tints the background inside the sprite's rectangle. With BlendState::NonPremultiplied the texel is invisible.

sources.note: compiled route: colour key, then premultiply; the build-versus-authored key comment

issues.evidence: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; not executed; the draw result follows from the blend equation. The pipeline comment records a deliberate difference (a build-requested key clears the colour, a .cnj-authored key keeps it, XNAP-96); on the compiled route premultiplication then clears it, so the runtime route is the only place where the kept colour reaches a draw. {{src:modules/content/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/CnjCacheIsolationTests.cpp|CnjCacheIsolationTests.cpp}} asserts cache isolation and alpha only.
issues.reproduction:
// Illustrative; not compiled or run. sprite.cnj: {"sourceFile": "sprite.png", "colorKey": [255, 0, 255]}
auto texture = content.Load<Texture2D>("sprite");
spriteBatch.Begin();                 // BlendState::AlphaBlend
spriteBatch.Draw(&texture, Vector2(0, 0), Color::White);
spriteBatch.End();
// Expected: keyed texels invisible. Actual by reading: background + (255, 0, 255).
issues.tests_current: CnjCacheIsolationTests.cpp (keyed alpha and cache isolation); no draw test of a keyed .cnj texture.
issues.regression_test: Load a keyed .cnj texture, draw it with the default SpriteBatch::Begin() over a known background, and read back: the keyed area must equal the background. The fix is writing Color(0, 0, 0, 0) in ApplyColorKey (or premultiplying on this route).
issues.blast_radius: Runtime-loaded .cnj Texture2D documents with colorKey drawn with a premultiplied blend state, typically ports of colour-keyed 2D games. Build-requested keys and compiled .cnb textures are unaffected.
issues.workaround: Draw such textures with BlendState::NonPremultiplied, or compile the document to .cnb.

issues.title: GraphicsDevice::GetMaxTextureDimension() is documented as the renderer's real maximum, but most renderers return an unqueried 16384 that the capability profile marks as known
issues.summary: Only VULKAN, DIRECT2D and GDI query a real limit; the other families inherit a constant 16384 (no GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE query), which the renderer capability profile nevertheless reports as a known limit.
issues.public_contract: GraphicsDevice::GetMaxTextureDimension() (CNAEXT); RendererLimit::MaxTextureDimension in the renderer capability profile
issues.expected: {{src:modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/GraphicsDevice.hpp|GraphicsDevice.hpp}}: “Returns the active renderer's real maximum single-axis texture dimension”, to be queried before accepting a caller- or file-supplied size so that the native API does not fail or corrupt memory.
issues.actual: IGraphicsRenderer::GetMaxTextureDimension in {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp|IGraphicsRenderer.hpp}} returns 16384, and its comment says no renderer overrides it. VULKAN (maxImageDimension2D), DIRECT2D (GetMaximumBitmapSize) and GDI (SoftwareFramebufferMaxDimension) do; FNA3D overrides to return the default. EasyGL, OPENGL4, SDL_GPU, WEBGPU and the rest inherit 16384 without asking the device; no GL renderer queries GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE. {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}} sets RendererLimit::MaxTextureDimension known whenever the value is non-negative, so a GLES or WebGL device limited to 4096 or 8192 is reported as 16384, and Texture2D's size check lets such a texture reach the native API.

issues.title: CNA has no counterpart of XNA's MissingVertexShaderInput draw check, and renderers resolve a stock-effect draw that lacks an input differently
issues.summary: XNA refuses a draw whose vertex declaration lacks a semantic the shader reads; CNA has no such check, so EasyGL/OPENGL4 feed neutral values, WEBGPU substitutes, SDL_GPU throws and VULKAN aliases TEXCOORD1.
issues.public_contract: GraphicsDevice::DrawPrimitives / DrawIndexedPrimitives / DrawUserPrimitives with a stock effect whose required vertex semantic is missing from the VertexDeclaration
issues.expected: The genuine XNA 4.0 GraphicsDevice refuses such a draw with InvalidOperationException (FrameworkResources.MissingVertexShaderInput, reached from its draw-time verification), identically on every device.
issues.actual: GraphicsDevice::validateDrawState in {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}} implements XNA's draw-time float-filtering and blending restrictions but no input check; no source under modules/ implements MissingVertexShaderInput. StockEffectUsesVertexSemantic in {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp|IGraphicsRenderer.hpp}} encodes the per-variant table but decides only which streams are consumed. EasyGL and OPENGL4 leave a missing attribute disabled and read the (0, 0, 0, 1) neutral record; WEBGPU's SelectStockVertexShapeEXT falls back from EnvironmentMapEffect without NORMAL0/TEXCOORD0 to a BasicEffect shape and sends alpha-test or dual-texture draws without TEXCOORD0 to the stride-16 coloured path; SDL_GPU throws NotSupportedException for those cases (std::invalid_argument for SkinnedEffect); VULKAN aliases TEXCOORD1 onto TEXCOORD0 for DualTextureEffect where the others read (0, 0).
issues.evidence: Checked by reading at 009d40f5 and the XNA 4.0 Graphics IL in the reference cache (MissingVertexShaderInput and its details string); not executed. The per-renderer outcomes are spot-checked at the named functions, not traced for every effect variant.

issues.regression_test: A renderer-independent test per stock effect variant that draws with a declaration missing one required semantic and expects InvalidOperationException before the renderer is reached.

issues.title: The registered CTest CNAEXT_NoPosixSetenv fails at this snapshot: twelve Wayland setenv/unsetenv call lines trip the gate
issues.summary: scripts/check_no_posix_setenv.py forbids POSIX setenv/unsetenv under modules/, tools/ and tests/, but the native Wayland backend and its tests added twelve such lines on 2026-09-15, so the gate CNA registers in every test-enabled tree exits 1.
issues.public_contract: CTest CNAEXT_NoPosixSetenv (modules/graphics-ext/examples/CMakeLists.txt, label CnaExt)
issues.expected: A gate CNA registers passes on its own tree. The rule it enforces (use System::Environment::SetEnvironmentVariable, because MinGW-w64 has no setenv/unsetenv) was introduced with the gate on 2026-08-19.
issues.actual: {{src:scripts/check_no_posix_setenv.py|check_no_posix_setenv.py}} reports twelve lines: ::unsetenv("XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN") in {{src:modules/platform/src/Wayland/WaylandPlatform.cpp|WaylandPlatform.cpp}}, and setenv/unsetenv of WAYLAND_SOCKET, WAYLAND_DISPLAY, LC_ALL, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS and XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN in WaylandDesktopPortalTests.cpp, WaylandProtocolTests.cpp, WaylandTestCompositor.cpp and WaylandTestEnvironment.cpp under {{src:modules/platform/tests/CNA/Platform/WaylandTestEnvironment.cpp|modules/platform/tests/CNA/Platform}}. The test is added in {{src:modules/graphics-ext/examples/CMakeLists.txt|graphics-ext/examples/CMakeLists.txt}} inside if(CNA_BUILD_TESTS) whenever a Python 3 interpreter is found, so it is red in every test-enabled tree. The Wayland code never reaches a Windows build, so the MinGW breakage the gate guards against does not occur; the defect is the permanently red gate. {{src:.github/workflows/general-tests-ci.yml|general-tests-ci.yml}} runs an unfiltered ctest and its known-failure list names only EasyGL_GraphicsDevice_ReferenceStencil, so that job would classify this failure as new.
